Theme

Money, work & business

insurance noun

also insure, insured, insurance policy, car insurance, health insurance, life insurance, insurance company

modern

Traupman 333: prō vītā cautiō, life insurance
M-O s.v. insurance: life insurance, vītae cautiō (after Egger)

cautiō, cautiōnis f.

noun, third declension

Classically a bond or security given against loss (Cic. Fam. 7.18.1; Lewis & Short); Traupman and Egger use it for insurance.

Other words

  • assēcūrātiō, assēcūrātiōnis f. — insurance

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · Traupman 333: assēcūrātiō vehiculāria, car insurance; assēcūrātiō valētūdināria, health insurance

    From sēcūrus; not in Lewis & Short.

  • mercēde pactā damnum vītāre — be insured: avoid a loss for an agreed fee

    verb phrase · also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 7

Examples

  • quōrum duo postulāta fuēre, ūnum ut mīlitiā vacārent dum in eō pūblicō essent, alterum ut quae in nāvēs imposuissent ab hostium tempestātisque vī pūblicō perīculō essent

    They made two demands: first, that they be free of military service while on this public contract; second, that whatever they put on board should be at the state’s risk against the enemy and stormsLiv. 23.49.1–2

  • Nam et negōtiātōribus certa lucra prōposuit susceptō in sē damnō, sī cui quid per tempestātēs accidisset

    He offered merchants a sure profit, taking the loss upon himself if storms brought anyone to griefSuet. Claud. 18.2

See also contract, bank, money.
